title: Small motor-carrier compliance & back-office hub (DOT compliance subscription → drug/alcohol consortium → IRP/title → bookkeeping/IFTA → insurance)
thesis: One buyer (owner of a 2–100-truck Chicago-area carrier; 25,049 active carriers in 8 counties per FMCSA census [A]) must buy several mandated recurring services. Enter with a DOT compliance subscription; cross-sell consortium membership, permits/plates, bookkeeping/IFTA, then commercial auto insurance once licensed. Compounding ARPU per account and a single sales motion.

title: Independent dental & veterinary practice operations bundle (managed IT + insurance verification/AR + OSHA/HIPAA compliance + spore testing + medical-waste pickup)
thesis: The practice office manager buys all five; each is recurring and low-capital. Bundling raises ARPU and switching costs. Consolidation by DSOs/corporate vet groups is the structural risk.

title: Restaurant back-of-house recurring service route (pest control + hood-filter exchange + dishmachine/chemical program + grease-trap service + draft-line cleaning)
thesis: Chicago has thousands of licensed food establishments with inspection-driven obligations. One technician route visiting the same kitchens monthly can stack several low-ticket recurring services, raising revenue per stop (route density economics).

title: Commercial energy cost management bundle (ICC-licensed electricity/gas brokerage + utility bill audit + demand-response enrollment + capacity-tag peak alerts)
thesis: PJM capacity prices at the cap in the ComEd zone make energy a CFO problem; one relationship can earn supplier commissions, contingency audit fees and demand-response revenue shares. Asset-light, recurring commission streams.

title: Workplace facility-services route, Cintas-lite (first-aid cabinet restocking + restroom hygiene + entrance mats + point-of-use water)
thesis: Cintas runs first aid & safety at ~25% operating margin [A]; a local van route can bundle several consumable/rental services into one weekly or monthly stop for small and mid-size workplaces.

title: Construction subcontractor back office (job-cost bookkeeping + prevailing-wage certified payroll + lien-rights administration + surety/insurance referrals)
thesis: Illinois public-works subcontractors must file certified payroll through IDOL and protect lien rights; the same owner needs job-cost bookkeeping and bonds. Recurring monthly fees, no license for the core, AI-assisted document work.

title: Chicago small-landlord operations plan (2–6 flats: maintenance & code-compliance plan + unit turns + porch/exterior repairs + landlord insurance referral)
thesis: Chicago's 2–6 flat stock faces porch, façade and code obligations; a maintenance-plan subscription with pull-through repair work and turn services can serve a dense, identifiable owner base.
